title: Low-volatility portfolio, monthly rebalanced, liquid NSE equities: research only, risk-adjusted alpha as the primary outcome, with an untouched held-out year
mechanism: Leverage-constrained and lottery-seeking investors overpay for high-volatility, high-beta stocks, so low-volatility stocks earn higher RISK-ADJUSTED returns than the market (Blitz and van Vliet 2007; Frazzini and Pedersen 2014, betting against beta; Baker, Bradley and Wurgler 2011). The claim is about alpha, not raw return: a low-volatility portfolio is expected to lag the market in strong rallies. Persistence in Indian equities after costs is NOT assumed.
disclosure: Before freezing, the author had seen: the desk's short-horizon breakout diagnosis (no stock-selection alpha against the equal-weight market, docs/research/loss_attribution_2026-11-21.md) and the 12-1 momentum discovery result (no alpha, beta 1.18, docs/research/momentum_12_1_discovery_2026-11-21.md). No return of THIS score on this data was computed before this file was frozen and committed.

universe.source: official NSE EQ bhavcopy store (offline SSD copy; delisted names included)
universe.membership: listed on or before the information cutoff and not delisted by it (universe_history.json); unknown membership is excluded, never assumed
universe.traded_price_note: judged on the price that traded on the cutoff day, not the back-adjusted price
universe.corporate_actions: back-adjusted on read; a rebalance is evaluated only when its whole formation window and holding period lie inside verified corporate-action coverage

score.definition: minus the sample standard deviation of daily log close-to-close returns over the formation window (sessions c-252 .. c), where c is the information cutoff (the official session before the rebalance session); bars up to c only; at least min_bars_in_formation finite returns
score.name: trailing 252-session volatility, lowest first

schedule.rebalance: first official session of each calendar month
schedule.information_cutoff: close of the previous official session
schedule.holding: until the close of the next rebalance session

portfolio.selection: the 20% of eligible names with the LOWEST trailing volatility

costs.basis: core.costs round trip 0.22% taxes and fees plus 0.10% slippage = 0.32%, charged on traded weight (turnover) at every rebalance

benchmark: equal-weight portfolio of ALL eligible names, rebalanced on the same schedule, gross of costs (conservative for the strategy)

held_out.rule: evaluated ONCE, after the discovery result is committed, with no rule changed; never used to choose anything

primary_outcome.statistic: monthly alpha: the intercept of the OLS regression of the portfolio's monthly NET return on the benchmark's monthly return
primary_outcome.test: one-sided t-test for alpha > 0 with a Newey-West (lag 1, Bartlett) covariance of the regression, alpha 0.05
primary_outcome.multiplicity: m = 1, outside the walk-forward BUY family and its alpha budget

secondary_outcomes: mean monthly NET excess return over the benchmark (expected negative in rallies; not a test)
Sharpe ratio of monthly net returns versus the benchmark's
count of held names that stopped trading during a holding period

missing_data.stopped_trading_during_holding: primary: the name's return to its last traded close, then cash; sensitivity: a further 50% and a 100% loss on the remainder; counts reported
missing_data.no_bar_on_rebalance_day: not executable: excluded from that rebalance

power.statement: Discovery spans about three years of monthly periods, so its power for a 0.5%/month alpha is LOW. An insignificant result is INCONCLUSIVE, not evidence of no alpha; a significant one needs the held-out year.

stopping: one discovery analysis and one held-out analysis; no early stop, no re-run with changed parameters
decision_on_result: PASS in discovery permits exactly one held-out evaluation. PASS on both is a proposal for an owner-approved paper experiment only: never a BUY, never a change to any gate, risk limit or admission rule.
